kept.claim: In the new list view (promRule only, no ruler rule) the "Silence notifications" menu item is shown but clicking it does nothing, because the drawer is gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) and rule is now undefined.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] "Silence notifications" is offered in the list view but the drawer can never open

**Severity:** HIGH — a visible, enabled action silently does nothing for every Grafana-managed alerting rule in the new list view.

### The Problem

`GrafanaRuleListItem` now renders `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} compact />` with no `rule` prop. `AlertRuleMenu` computes `canSilence` as `(ruler) || (grafanaSilenceSupported && grafanaSilenceAllowed)`, and `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` returns `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` for prom rules, so the menu item is rendered. Clicking it calls `handleSilence` -> `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`, but the drawer is rendered only when:

```tsx
{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && (
  <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} onClose={() => setShowSilenceDrawer(false)} />
)}
```

`rule` is `undefined` here, so the condition is always false.

### Theory / Proof

- `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:48` passes only `promRule`.
- `AlertRuleMenu.tsx:124-130` renders the Silence item whenever `canSilence` is true.
- `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104` requires a ruler rule to mount the drawer.
- The new test `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` ("should render correct menu actions") asserts the silence item exists but never clicks it, so the dead action is not caught.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Before this PR every list item had a ruler rule, so the drawer opened. After it, the list view has no ruler rule, so the button stays visible and clicking it has no effect and shows no error.

### Research

`SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` only needs the rule UID to pre-fill the `__alert_rule_uid__` matcher. The prom DTO already carries `uid`, so the ruler DTO is not required.

### Recommendation

Let the drawer accept a rule UID (or a prom rule) and render it from either source:

```tsx
const silenceRuleUid = rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)
  ? rule.grafana_alert.uid
  : prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(promRule)
    ? promRule.uid
    : undefined;

{silenceRuleUid && showSilenceDrawer && (
  <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer ruleUid={silenceRuleUid} onClose={() => setShowSilenceDrawer(false)} />
)}
```

Also add a test that clicks the menu item and asserts the drawer opens.
kept.evidence: GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:47 passes only promRule; AlertRuleMenu.tsx:126-131 renders Silence when the prom ability is true (useAbilities.ts:323); RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104 mounts the drawer only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule), and rule is undefined; the test only checks that the item is present. SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer only uses the uid.

kept.claim: Pause and Delete are still gated on rulerRule in AlertRuleMenu, so the new prom-only list view can never show them even though useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities computes grafanaPauseAbility/grafanaDeleteAbility; the new test locks in only 4 menu items.
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Pause and Delete disappear from the new list view; the prom-based abilities for them are computed but unused

**Severity:** MEDIUM — users with edit/delete permissions lose the Pause/Resume and Delete actions from the rule list.

### The Problem

The PR adds `grafanaPauseAbility` and `grafanaDeleteAbility` and ORs them into `canPause`/`canDelete`, but rendering still requires a ruler rule:

```tsx
{canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana' && (
  <MenuItemPauseRule rule={rulerRule} ... />
)}
...
{canDelete && rulerRule && ( ... handleDelete(rulerRule, groupIdentifier) ... )}
```

The list view (`GrafanaRuleListItem`) now passes only `promRule`, so `rulerRule` is always `undefined` and neither item renders, whatever the permissions.

### Theory / Proof

- `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:48` passes no `rule`, and `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:95` forwards `rulerRule={rule}` (undefined).
- `AlertRuleMenu.tsx:123` and `:165` check `rulerRule`.
- The new test `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` grants `AlertingRuleUpdate`/`AlertingRuleDelete` and still asserts `menuItems.length).toBe(4)` (silence, copy link, duplicate, export). That confirms Pause and Delete are gone even for fully privileged users.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Before: list items had ruler rules, so Pause and Delete appeared. After: they are silently removed, and the prom-side ability plumbing for them is dead code.

### Research

`MenuItemPauseRule` and `useDeleteModal` both work from a rule UID plus group identifier. The ruler DTO is fetched only to rebuild the group for the update call. That can be done lazily on click (fetch the ruler group, then mutate), which keeps the ruler API off the list page's initial render.

### Recommendation

Either make the prom path fully functional or remove the dead abilities. For example:

```tsx
{canPause && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana' && (rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) || prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)) && (
  <MenuItemPauseRule ruleUid={rulerRule?.grafana_alert.uid ?? promRule.uid} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} onPauseChange={onPauseChange} />
)}
```

Have `MenuItemPauseRule` and the delete handler fetch the ruler group on demand. Update the test to expect Pause and Delete when the permissions are granted.
kept.evidence: AlertRuleMenu.tsx:123 needs rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) and :165 needs rulerRule; the list path (GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:70, FilterView.tsx:157 -> GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:47) never passes a ruler rule; the test grants update/delete but expects 4 items. V2's handleDelete ignores the rulerRule argument, so only Pause truly needs the ruler DTO.

kept.claim: Because useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities with isFederated hard-coded to false, the legacy RuleActionsButtons (rule list table and rule viewer) now shows the Edit button for rules in federated (source_tenants) Mimir groups, which it hid before.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Edit button now shown for rules in federated (Mimir) rule groups in the legacy list and rule viewer

**Severity:** MEDIUM — the Edit action is offered for federated rules, which the UI deliberately hid before because the editor cannot represent `source_tenants` groups.

### The Problem

Before:
```ts
const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group);
```
After, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`, which hard-codes:
```ts
// TODO: Add support for federated rules
const isFederated = false;
```
`rule.group.source_tenants` is still available in the wrapper but is no longer passed down, so `immutableRule` is false and `AlertRuleAction.Update` becomes supported.

### Theory / Proof

- `isFederatedRuleGroup` (`utils/rules.ts:373`) returns true when `source_tenants` is set.
- `components/rules/RuleActionsButtons.tsx:57` reads `useAlertRuleAbility(rule, AlertRuleAction.Update)` to decide whether to render the Edit button. That component is used in `RulesTable.tsx:329` and `RuleViewer.tsx:126`.
- `ExistingRuleEditor` only shows a `FederatedRuleWarning` and still renders the form, so nothing further down stops an edit.
- Group-level editing (`RulesGroup.tsx:61`) still checks federation, so rule-level and group-level behaviour now disagree.

Note: Delete in `AlertRuleMenu` already went through `useRulerRuleAbilities`, which hard-coded `isFederated = false` before this PR. The regression introduced here is the Edit button.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Before: federated rules showed no Edit button. After: users with external rule write permission see Edit on them and can open the editor, which cannot preserve federated-group semantics.

### Research

Mimir federated rule groups: https://grafana.com/docs/mimir/latest/references/architecture/components/ruler/#federated-rule-groups. The new prom-based hook correctly says Grafana-managed rules cannot be federated, but the CombinedRule path also covers data source (Mimir) rules.

### Recommendation

Pass the federation flag through from the CombinedRule wrapper:

```ts
export function useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule): Abilities<AlertRuleAction> {
  const groupIdentifierV2 = useMemo(() => groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule(rule), [rule]);
  return useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2, { isFederated: isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) });
}
```
and use `options?.isFederated ?? false` inside `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`.
kept.evidence: Base useAllAlertRuleAbilities used isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group); HEAD delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities with isFederated=false (useAbilities.ts:242-245). The legacy RuleActionsButtons.tsx:57 Update ability (RulesTable.tsx:329, RuleViewer.tsx:126) now shows Edit for federated rules. Delete was already unguarded through useRulerRuleAbilities before the PR; Pause/Restore are Grafana-only.
kept.corrected_claim: Because useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities with isFederated hard-coded to false, the legacy RuleActionsButtons (rule list table and rule viewer) now shows the Edit button for rules in federated (source_tenants) Mimir groups, which it hid before.

kept.claim: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates ModifyExport on grafana.alertingRule instead of grafana.rule, so Grafana recording rules lose the Export menu item in the new list view. Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently use the same predicate but show no visible effect today.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Grafana recording rules lose the Export action in the new list view

**Severity:** LOW — a feature regression for recording rules in the list; the Export item is still shown on the rule detail page.

### The Problem

```ts
// All GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed by definition
const isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule);
...
[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed],
```

The ruler equivalent uses `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which matches both alerting and recording rules. The comment says "Grafana-managed" but the code checks "alerting".

### Theory / Proof

`prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule` (`utils/rules.ts:134`) excludes recording rules. In the list view `GrafanaRuleListItem` passes only `promRule`, so every ruler ability in `AlertRuleMenu` is false and `canExport` depends only on this prom ability. For Grafana recording rules it is false, so Export disappears. Before the PR, the list passed `rulerRule` and Export was shown.

Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently use the same predicate. They have no visible effect today (Pause still needs `rulerRule` in the menu), but they will once the prom path is wired up.

### Recommendation

```ts
const isGrafanaManagedRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule);
const isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule);
...
[AlertRuleAction.Silence]: [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule],
[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isGrafanaManagedRule, exportAllowed],
[AlertRuleAction.Pause]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, isEditable ?? false],
[AlertRuleAction.Restore]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, isEditable ?? false],
```
kept.evidence: useAbilities.ts:301 uses grafana.alertingRule, while the ruler version uses grafana.rule. In the list only the prom ability counts, so recording rules lose Export. Pause still needs rulerRule in the menu, and Restore/DeletePermanently are not read from the prom hook.
kept.corrected_claim: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates ModifyExport on grafana.alertingRule instead of grafana.rule, so Grafana recording rules lose the Export menu item in the new list view. Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently use the same predicate but show no visible effect today.

kept.claim: The rewritten GrafanaRuleListItem drops the returnTo query param (createReturnTo()) from the rule view link, so navigating from the list to a rule and back loses the current list filters/search, unlike the removed implementation and DataSourceRuleListItem.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Rule view link no longer carries `returnTo`

**Severity:** LOW — a UX regression: after opening a rule from a filtered list, "back" does not return to the filtered list.

### The Problem

Removed code (`GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`):
```tsx
const returnTo = createReturnTo();
href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }),
```
New code:
```tsx
href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`),
```

### Theory / Proof

`DataSourceRuleListItem.tsx:36-42` still builds its link with `createReturnTo()`, so data source rules and Grafana rules now behave differently in the same list. The rule viewer uses `returnTo` to go back to the list with the original filter and search query string.

### What happens today vs. what will break

A user filters the list (for example `?search=state:firing`), opens a Grafana rule, and clicks back or the breadcrumb. They land on the unfiltered list. Data source rules keep the filter.

### Recommendation

```tsx
import { createReturnTo } from '../hooks/useReturnTo';
...
const returnTo = createReturnTo();
...
href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }),
```
kept.evidence: GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:40 has no returnTo; the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader and DataSourceRuleListItem.tsx:36-42 use createReturnTo(); RuleViewer.tsx:96 reads useReturnTo('/alerting/list') for the back button.
